approach: Fix where the fault starts: a check killed at its deadline is recorded like a real failure, so the verdict rejects the job. (1) Raise check_timeout_s to 1800 in athena.toml; config.rs is untouched. (2) In checks.rs add one shared deadline note (`deadline_note(limit_s)`, used by run_check) and `timed_out(&CheckRun)` (exit_code None and note starts with that text), plus `held_for_timeout(&[CheckRun]) -> Option<(name, secs)>`, which returns Some only when at least one check failed and every failed check timed out. (3) In disk.rs add `CHECK_TIMEOUT = "environment: check timed out"`, a reason builder that carries the measured duration and the limit ('905s of 900s limit') and `athena retry <job>`, and make `is_environment_reason` accept it, so `resumable_stop` and the resume-mark logic (`settle_resume_marks`) follow without more change. (4) In `check_and_verify` (run/mod.rs), after the 'checks' line, when `held_for_timeout` is Some and the checks were not resumed, close with `self.failure(...)` as the low-disk stop before the verifier does (keep changed_paths, verification_passed None, remove the verify dir, return). If any check failed for real, the job proceeds and is rejected as today. (5) In status.rs add `CheckDurations` (median, slowest, count, limit, flag when slowest > 0.8 × limit) computed from stored `verification.checks` of the newest 20 request jobs with a check named `test`; add it to StatusView, read the limit from `JobConfig::at(..).config.budget.check_timeout_s` (already loaded in `status()`), and give it a `text()`. (6) Print it in `display::status` (crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs); that file is not in the brief's deliverables but is the only place that prints `athena status` (see open_questions). (7) CHANGELOG entry citing 20261026-232434-6wfq. Tests drive the real `Athena::go` through the existing `produce_and_verify_order_tests` harness; a cfg(test) `check_seam` (same pattern as `replay_seam`) swaps only the check process, so classification and closing stay in production code.

decisions.choice: Classify by the shared deadline note plus exit_code None (`timed_out`), with the note text built by one function used by both run_check and the classifier.
decisions.reason: CheckRun gains no field (out of scope). One function for the text means the writer and the reader cannot drift. The kill-switch note and 'ran zero tests' have other notes, so they are not mistaken for a timeout.

rejected.why: Out of scope, and it changes the record schema and AnyRecord handling.

rejected.option: Match the text 'killed at the deadline' separately in run/mod.rs
rejected.why: Duplicated string that can drift from checks.rs.

decisions.choice: Hold the job as an environment stop only when every failed check timed out (`held_for_timeout`); any real failure leaves the normal path to rejection.
decisions.reason: Review finding (b) of the earlier attempt: a timeout must not hide a real failure in another check.

rejected.option: Hold whenever any check timed out
rejected.why: Would let a real failure be retried away instead of rejected.

decisions.choice: Reason prefix `environment: check timed out`, recognised in `is_environment_reason`.
decisions.reason: It starts with ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX ('environment:'), so scope_guard's prefix test still ties. `resumable_stop` and `settle_resume_marks` already key on `is_environment_reason`, so `athena retry` resumes from the kept candidate with no other change.

rejected.why: Schema change; the Failed + environment reason mechanism exists.

decisions.choice: Test seam: cfg(test) thread-local `check_seam` in lib.rs, read first in `SnapExec::exec` in place of `run_check`.
decisions.reason: Matches `replay_seam`. The fake returns only a CheckRun (exit None, the shared deadline note, duration 905 s). The decision logic runs in production code. Waiting for a real 900 s kill is not feasible, and the seam is per thread so parallel tests stay isolated.

rejected.option: A real sleep with check_timeout_s = 1 in the test config
rejected.why: Gives '1s of 1s limit', not the 905/900 case, adds a 5 s kill grace, and gives no exact duration. A cheap real-kill assertion of `timed_out` is kept in checks.rs instead.

decisions.choice: Status durations come from stored `verification.checks` of the newest 20 request jobs (sorted by id), skipping jobs with no check named `test`; limit = configured check_timeout_s.
decisions.reason: Matches the accepted reading; no new record. Median of an even count is the mean of the two middle values; the flag is `slowest > 0.8 × limit`.

rejected.option: Parse durations out of closing reasons
rejected.why: Fragile text parsing, and still no check record for held jobs.

decisions.choice: Add `check_durations: Option<CheckDurations>` to StatusView (serialised, so `status --json` shows it) with `text()` in status.rs; display.rs only appends that text.
decisions.reason: Keeps the logic in the deliverable file and the CLI change to a few lines.

rejected.why: It is a report, not a next action.

risks.risk: A genuinely hung check is retried forever as an environment stop and never rejected.
risks.mitigation: The stop is a Failed job needing a manual `athena retry`, not an automatic loop. The reason names the check, the duration and the limit, and the status report flags near-limit checks at 80%.

risks.risk: The fake could hide a wrong classification if it set the same text the classifier reads.
risks.mitigation: The note comes from the shared `checks::deadline_note`, and a checks.rs test uses a real `run_check` kill (300 ms limit, as the existing baseline timeout test does) to show `timed_out` is true for a real kill. The fake only supplies the record.

risks.risk: Adding a StatusView field breaks other constructors or JSON expectations.
risks.mitigation: The only StatusView literal is in `status()`. The field is `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`, so JSON for repositories without test checks is unchanged. fmt, clippy and the full test run cover the rest.

risks.risk: Raising the limit to 1800 s lets a truly stuck check use the verifier's snapshot and disk for 30 minutes.
risks.mitigation: This is the requested value. The kill still happens at the deadline, and the disk gate before the verifier is unchanged.

risks.risk: The resume mark for a held job stays at stage Checks, so a retry reruns all the checks.
risks.mitigation: That is intended: no passing check results exist to reuse. `settle_resume_marks` keeps the mark for environment reasons, so the retry skips the planner and producer.

demonstrations.method: Content check by reading the two files.
demonstrations.command: grep -n "check_timeout_s" athena.toml crates/athena-data/src/config.rs  (Grep tool; the verifier may also run `git diff --stat`, which must not list crates/athena-data)
demonstrations.observes: athena.toml has `check_timeout_s = 1800`. config.rs line 234 still reads `pub check_timeout_s: u64` and its validation is not in the diff.

demonstrations.method: New test `a_check_killed_at_its_deadline_closes_as_an_environment_stop` in `produce_and_verify_order_tests` (crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs). Entry point: `Athena::go` on a job made by `athena.ask(..)` in the existing harness (`athena_with`, the `Docs` capability, the fake agent script). Preconditions: plenty of disk (`test_support::plenty_of_space`), checks not resumed, not nested. Seam: `crate::check_seam::install(..)` (added by step 2; it does not exist today) returns a CheckRun with exit_code None, passed false, note `checks::deadline_note(900)`, duration 905 s. The fake builds the record only; the classification, closing and state come from production code. It asserts: state Failed (not Rejected), `disk::is_environment_reason(&reason)`, `disk::resumable_stop(JobState::Closed(Failed), Some(&reason))`, and no verifier invocation (Counts verifier == 0).
demonstrations.observes: The job closes Failed with an environment reason, is resumable, and the verifier never ran.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `held_for_timeout` early return the job continues to the verifier, `judge` sees a failed check and the state is Rejected, so the Failed/environment assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Two parts. (a) Job-level test `a_real_nonzero_check_failure_is_still_rejected` in the same module: no seam, capability check `false` (a real exit 1), `Athena::go` ends Rejected and `is_environment_reason` is false; this contrasts with test 2. (b) Unit test `held_for_timeout_needs_every_failed_check_to_have_timed_out` in checks.rs: [timed-out, exit-1] and [exit-1, timed-out] give None, [timed-out] gives Some, a failure with the kill-switch note gives None, and all-pass gives None. A mixed set cannot arise from local runs, because `run_local` stops at the first failure; it can arise only from CI-reused records, so this is tested at the function `check_and_verify` calls. A third test, `a_job_whose_checks_include_a_real_failure_is_rejected_even_if_the_seam_times_out`, installs a seam that returns a timeout for one spec and uses the real failing command for the other; it is added only if the `Docs` capability can hold two checks (open question).
demonstrations.observes: A real nonzero exit leaves the job Rejected, and any set with a real failure is not held.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the hold ignored real failures (any timed-out check holds), the mixed cases in (b) would return Some, and a real failure could be retried instead of rejected.

demonstrations.method: In test 2, also capture the UI lines with the harness `Lines` UI and assert both the closing `reason` and the printed `failed     ` line contain `905s of 900s limit`. A pure unit test in disk.rs, `check_timeout_reason_names_the_duration_and_the_limit`, asserts the builder output 'environment: check timed out: test ran 905s of 900s limit; this is the environment, not the work. Run `athena retry <job>`'. The limit passed is `jc.config.budget.check_timeout_s`, and the test config is 900 only if the test repo sets it; otherwise the seam's note uses the configured limit read from the repo config. The plan fixes the test repo's limit to 900 by replacing the `check_timeout_s` line in `repo()` text for this test.
demonstrations.observes: Both the stored reason and the printed line carry the measured duration and the limit.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the reason omitted the duration or limit, or used a different format, the `905s of 900s limit` substring assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: New test in status.rs (`check_durations_report_median_slowest_and_the_eighty_percent_flag`). Entry points: `check_durations(&Records, limit_s)` and `CheckDurations::text()`, the same functions `Athena::status()` calls to fill `StatusView.check_durations`. Fixture: a `Records` seeded with 22 request jobs, each with `verification` built as in the existing status.rs test near line 2088, and a check named `test` with a chosen duration. The oldest 2 jobs have huge durations to show that only the newest 20 count. One job has no `test` check and is skipped. Case A: slowest 1500 s against 1800 gives `flagged` true and a text containing the median, the slowest and the limit. Case B: slowest 1000 s gives no flag. Case C: exactly 1440 s (80%) is not flagged. Plus a CLI test in display.rs, `status_prints_the_check_durations_line`, that builds a StatusView from `Athena::status()` on a seeded repo or a small literal and asserts `display::status` contains the line only when `check_durations` is Some. If a literal is too large, the status.rs `text()` assertion carries the criterion and the display test only checks the line is appended.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-core check_durations_report_median_slowest_and_the_eighty_percent_flag  &&  cargo test --locked -p athena-cli status_prints_the_check_durations_line
demonstrations.observes: Printed text shows median and slowest over the last 20 jobs against the limit, with the flag exactly when slowest exceeds 80% of the limit.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the computation there is no line. With a wrong window (all jobs) the median and slowest differ from the expected values. With a wrong threshold, Case C or B flips.

open_questions: display.rs (athena-cli) and lib.rs (athena-core, test seam) are not in the brief's deliverables list, but 'athena status prints' cannot hold without display.rs and the fake check runner needs the lib.rs seam. A held job writes no verification record (same as the low-disk stop), so its test-check duration never enters the status report. The report therefore shows only jobs whose checks finished, and the jobs closest to the limit are the ones most likely to be missing. Accepted per the reading; a later change could record the check run.

Whether the `Docs` test capability can hold two checks for the combined timeout-and-real-failure job test. Its `check` field is one command today. If not, criterion 3's mixed case is shown at the `held_for_timeout` function that `check_and_verify` calls. Local runs stop at the first failed check (`run_local`), so a mixed set arises only from CI-reused records.
Which existing test loads athena.toml (criterion 7) was not located; the `repo()` helper in run/mod.rs tests includes athena.toml, and the producer should name the config test in its report.

The test repo's limit: the plan sets check_timeout_s to 900 in the `repo()` text for the timeout test so the message reads '905s of 900s limit'. The producer may instead pass the limit through the seam's note. Either way the limit printed must be the configured one.
